title: Session handoff: #486 at 8e811a5a with the QCLI-433 union applied, binaries stale pending a ruling
description:
Session handoff for the successor, 2026-10-02, written at opum-agent's instruction for the recycle gate (their seq 169 said: write the handoff, push it, say gate-ready).

WHERE THE WORK IS. opum-ai/quest-cli#486 is OPEN against dev, head 8e811a5a47c2d782210b104f34a8241f97a2c7b4 on branch chore/QCLI-433-bump-0-13-0, pushed and read back from BOTH the ref and the PR headRefOid (they agreed). That SHA is the final 0.13.0 tree and it is what lore-cli's QUEST_SOURCE_REF should point at. dev is e2728aa4.

WHAT LANDED WHILE GETTING THERE: #489 (board full-screen, QCLI-435) at baa10e37, #490 (migrate-from-backlog skill, QCLI-436) at bea76848, #491 (tracker bookkeeping) at fda5efb5. QCLI-435 and QCLI-436 are Done with every criterion checked against evidence and no unresolvedAtCompletion field. The merge into #486 applied the QCLI-433 union: five notes (this branch's three evidence notes plus dev's pause note and release note, both verified byte-for-byte by sha256) and status Paused.

THE ONE THING THAT NEEDS A DECISION BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE TOUCHES #486: THE SIX COMMITTED PLATFORM BINARIES ARE STALE FOR THIS TREE, and opum-agent has the report and has not answered. Measured, not inferred -- `bun build src/cli/main.ts` on the merged tree produces a bundle containing the string `migrate-from-backlog`, which src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts added and the 7f567a67 binaries predate; exactly one file under src/ differs from the bytes head and it is imported by the compile entrypoint. **Do not rebuild until opum-agent rules.** Rebuilding is a CI dispatch (prepublication-qualification against the branch), because bun cannot cross-compile win32-arm64 and a local macOS build risks the darwin-arm64 code-signing hazard in docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md.

THE HOLD, UNCHANGED. Change nothing on #486 until opum-agent reports that lore 0.13.0 is on npm. Checked live at handoff time: @opum-ai/lore dist-tags read latest 0.12.0 and the versions list ends 0.12.0, so the hold was still in force. Then, in order: lore-cli's LCLI-665 moves its QUEST_SOURCE_REF to a verified quest-cli commit carrying 0.13.0 (8e811a5a is the candidate, but re-read whatever #486 heads at by then); lore 0.13.0 is tagged and published through the operator's own dialog in lore-cli; the lore-check pin at .github/workflows/lore-check.yml:159 moves from @opum-ai/lore@0.12.0 to 0.13.0 and RIDES IN #486 rather than a follow-up; then #486 can go green and land. The pin move must regenerate the committed .lore schemas with that same lore and measure the regenerated tree with `npx --yes @opum-ai/lore@0.13.0` before choosing the landing shape, exactly as QCLI-422 did.

TIER 3, after that, in this repository's own dialog and none of it started: the Unreleased -> 0.13.0 changelog rename with a fresh successor heading at tag time; the v0.13.0 tag; the receipt-gated publish staged under release-candidate, after lore-cli's main reads 0.13.0 and the operator authorizes; receipt:verify-published; and the dev-to-main fast-forward promotion. Nothing is tagged, staged, published or promoted.

OPEN AND UNRULED: QCLI-437, the `--source <project>` help text. Not prose-only -- command-contract.ts:740 derives each manifest entry's positionals from the same usage string, so renaming <project> to <path> renames the positional in `quest manifest --json` from project to path. opum-agent has it; left out of 0.13.0.

OUT OF SCOPE, DECIDED (opum-agent seq 169): kanban card movement is NOT in 0.13.0. 0.13.0 ships the read-only kanban as built. Movement comes next release, by keyboard, mapped to Quest's lifecycle commands; opum-doc will issue the design. Do not start it.

RELEASE NOTE ALREADY RECORDED ON QCLI-433, so the notes can be written from it rather than re-derived: a workspace installing 0.13.0 sees `quest agents --check` report DRIFT until it runs `quest agents --update-instructions`, because the quest skill is generated and the migrate-from-backlog pointer reaches both generated variants.

ARTIFACTS. /tmp/qcli433-artifacts holds the six CI-built packages from qualification run 37073166852, downloaded 2026-10-02. That run's retention is 7 days, so they expire around 2026-10-09; after that, re-dispatch prepublication-qualification.yml against the branch.

ALSO OPEN, ADJACENT. The board build choices -- the across-refs toggle, repository discovery through userConfig, the uncommitted-window banner, and the Reference layout -- were under opum-doc review and must not change while it runs (operator instruction 2026-10-02, opum-agent OPAG-1086).

SKILLS THE SUCCESSOR SHOULD REACH FOR: opum-sdlc before branch or merge work, docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md for the tag-time steps and the darwin-arm64 execution ordering, opum-quest for tracker writes, opum-lore for the bundle, opum-handoff to restore.

ONE OPERATIONAL TRAP MEASURED THIS SESSION, worth more than it costs to read: the required-check wait raced registration TWICE in the same direction. A background loop over the check-runs API read all three required contexts completed/success and exited; seconds later the two-predicate gate returned newest-per-context true but no-required-row-pending FALSE, because a second source-gates row registered after the loop concluded. Require the settled answer twice, a gap apart, and run the gate as its own call.
implementationNotes:
HANDOFF REFRESHED AFTER THE RECYCLE ORDER, 2026-10-03T00:2x UTC. The orchestrator ordered this recycle and asked for a handoff written AFTER that order, so this note supersedes the description above where the two differ. Read this note first; everything in the description still holds except the two points below.

NOTHING CHANGED SINCE THE DESCRIPTION, and that is the report. Verified live at this writing rather than assumed: dev is c0d5fd29 (level with origin/dev, clean working tree, this session checked out on dev). opum-ai/quest-cli#486 is OPEN, unparked and UNTOUCHED — head still 8e811a5a47c2d782210b104f34a8241f97a2c7b4, the same SHA reported to opum-agent as the final 0.13.0 tree for lore-cli's QUEST_SOURCE_REF. The handoff record QCLI-438 was landed on dev by #492 (merged 3c3d0ef4) rather than left in an open PR, so a branch-scoped restore finds it.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE DESCRIPTION'S FRAMING, both minor and both measured:

1. The description says "#489 ... #490 ... #491" landed; add #492 for the handoff record itself. dev's tip is #492's squash, c0d5fd29.

2. The check-registration trap in the description is stated as a caution; it is better stated as a rule. The two-predicate gate must be run as its OWN call after any wait loop, and the settled answer must hold TWICE a gap apart, because a loop that reports its own success is the thing the gate exists to catch. Measured twice in one session: PR #490's wait exited "SETTLED" and the gate minutes later read newest-per-context true but no-required-row-pending FALSE, because a second source-gates row registered after the loop concluded. Waiting is what caught it — no merge moved on a stale-clean read.

STILL OPEN AND UNRULED, unchanged: QCLI-437 (the `--source <project>` help text, which is not prose-only because command-contract.yml's contract derives positionals from the same usage string) and the STALE PLATFORM BINARIES, which opum-agent has with the measurement and has not ruled on. Do not rebuild the binaries, and do not touch #486, until that ruling arrives and until lore 0.13.0 is on npm.

NOTHING IS IN PROGRESS. QCLI-433 is Paused (parked deliberately, its union resolved); QCLI-435 and QCLI-436 are Done; QCLI-438 is this handoff. No task was left mid-flight, and no branch was deleted: chore/QCLI-433-bump-0-13-0 and chore/QCLI-438-handoff-note are both left exactly as they were, as instructed.

STALE PLATFORM BINARIES carry the old QCLI-437 help text; the checksum gate cannot see it. Appended 2026-10-12 from the DEC-172 (4bg) filing PR. This updates the "STALE PLATFORM BINARIES" item the description and the 2026-10-03 note both left open with opum-agent: it is no longer only "stale relative to a merged tree", it is now a stale STRING in the artifact a user runs.

Found by QCLI-437's review, re-measured here rather than carried. Five of the six committed platform binaries still embed the pre-fix help string `--source <project>` (three occurrences each): linux-x64, linux-arm64, darwin-x64, win32-x64 and win32-arm64, read from the stored blobs with `git cat-file blob` (darwin-arm64 was deliberately not read, to avoid the AMFI code-signing SIGKILL this repository's profile documents). Against that, `grep -- '--source <project>' src/` is now 0 and src/application/command-help.ts:109/:122 and src/application/agents/guides.ts:485 carry `--source <path>`. The source rename therefore does not reach a shipped binary until the next platform rebuild.

Why the existing gate passes it: scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs hashes each committed binary and compares the digest ONLY against the checksum map (manifest.questBinarySha256 and rootPackage.questPlatformPackages[...]). The map is regenerated from those same committed binaries, so it always agrees with them; nothing in the check rebuilds from current source and compares. A binary stale relative to src/ passes by construction.

Consequence: the published 0.13.0 still prints `<project>` for `quest migration backlog --source`, and so will the next release unless the six platform binaries are rebuilt for the tree that ships. No rebuild was triggered here — this is a note, and the rebuild decision belongs to a release, not to this filing.
